title: Random force gives cubic phase variance at Keplerian shear in an ideal charged-dust model
abstract: We test whether radial grain stability preserves a narrow cloud in longitude near stellar corotation. We add random acceleration to a published local charged-dust model in which one shearing gas sets drag and the ideal electric field. At Keplerian shear, with decaying nonzero modes, we derive longitude variance equal to (2/3) Q^2 D_c tau^3 at late local times. The coefficient D_c includes signed field and drag. Above Keplerian shear the late variance is linear; exact finite-time covariance resolves its apparently divergent coefficient near the boundary. Shared forcing moves a cloud, while independent forcing broadens it. A reset model gives a stationary width proportional to the cube of mean grain age. Projection identities, an independent covariance solver and a 10,000-grain simulation check the result. An illustrative 1 micrometre thermal grain takes about 11,240 rotations to reach 0.15 rad, so this study does not establish short thermal lifetimes. Shear dispersion and orbital dust diffusion are prior results; the contribution is the explicit magnetic coefficient, transition and conditional coherence test. We infer no observed force strength, material lifetime or CPV rate. All bundled outputs are synthetic and need no external data.
